title: Simplification Rules for Continuous-Time Quantum Walks on Dynamic Graphs
authors: Mostafa Atallah, Daniel Dilley, Jishnu Mahmud, Zain H Saleem, Rebekah Herrman
abstract: Continuous-time quantum walks (CTQWs) on dynamic graphs realize quantum gates as sequences of time-evolving graph Hamiltonians, but naive constructions produce long sequences with redundancy. Simplification rules, which are graph rewrite rules that shorten a dynamic graph sequence while preserving the unitary it implements, are the CTQW analogue of circuit identities in the gate model. In this work, we give CTQW realizations of the standard single-qubit gates and introduce new graph rewrite rules. We demonstrate the simplification rules through worked circuit reductions and outline their use as transpilation primitives for converting between the circuit model and the dynamic graph framework.
summary: This paper introduces simplification rules for Continuous-Time Quantum Walks (CTQWs) on dynamic graphs, treating these rules as the CTQW equivalent of circuit identities. By developing these rewrite rules, the authors show how complex sequences of time-evolving Hamiltonians can be drastically shortened while preserving the implemented quantum unitary. This offers a new, compact framework for representing and compiling quantum circuits.
main_problem: The primary goal is to develop simplification rules for Continuous-Time Quantum Walks (CTQWs) on dynamic graphs to significantly shorten the sequence of time-evolving Hamiltonians required to implement a specific unitary transformation.
main_result: The authors successfully derived new graph rewrite rules and demonstrated that standard single-qubit gates, as well as the $n$-th root of any single-qubit gate, can be realized efficiently within the CTQW framework.
method: The work involves deriving and applying graph rewrite rules (simplification techniques) to the time evolution operator, which is calculated as the time-ordered exponential of a sequence of time-dependent graph Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The system is Continuous-Time Quantum Walks (CTQWs) operating on dynamic graphs. The dynamics are governed by the time evolution operator $e^{-iA_{total}t}$, where $A_{total}$ is constructed from a sequence of time-evolving graph Hamiltonians derived from the graph's adjacency matrix.
key_observables: The implemented unitary transformation (e.g., Identity, $P(	heta)$, $R_x(\alpha)$), and the resulting simplified graph sequence.
important_parameters: Time evolution times ($t$), graph structure (adjacency matrices $A$), and angular parameters ($	heta, \phi, \lambda, \alpha$).
main_assumptions: The list of simplification rules presented is not claimed to be exhaustive, and the framework assumes the equivalence between the circuit model and the dynamic graph model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the realization of specific gates (like Identity and $P(	heta)$) using dynamic graph sequences, and later figures demonstrate the simplification of complex sequences (like $X$ gate evolution) into shorter, equivalent forms.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the context of CTQWs as a universal quantum computation model. It then details the construction of fundamental gates ($iI, -iI, P(	heta)$) using specific graph sequences. The core of the work introduces and proves several graph rewrite rules (Observations IV.1-IV.5) to simplify these sequences, culminating in the realization of general gates and roots.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, graph-theoretic analogue to circuit identities, which is highly relevant for quantum information theorists developing efficient quantum compilation and transpilation tools.
